summary: CCC-era wooden tower (1939) replaced by a 91-ft steel tower; CalFire staffed it for decades; county radio and a Crown Castle tower share the site.

Listed as an Aircraft Warning Service Station
Viola Eldredge serving as lookout, August 1958
91-foot steel tower replaced the wooden tower. Register description and Peakbagging give 1959; a 1974 article and the Weebly page give 1958
California Division of Forestry leasing the site; land then owned by Cloverdale Redwood Company
Masonite Corporation acquired the land and continued the lease
Masonite Corporation announced it was deeding the site to the State of California
County emergency communications operated from the site since 1980

corrections.why: The register and Peakbagging give 91 ft (27.7 m) for the steel tower standing today. 27.4 m is 90 ft, the height the 1974 article gives for the earlier wooden tower.

The register's description dates the first CCC tower to 1939. The 1960 in the register's Built field belongs to the steel tower, which its description and Peakbagging date to 1959. A 1974 article quoted on the Weebly page dates the wooden tower to 1942, which disputes 1939.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 90-foot figure in the 1974 article describes the earlier wooden tower. The 91-foot steel tower is the one standing today.
The register's Built field says 1960, but its own description and Peakbagging give 1959 for the steel tower. The story uses 1959 for the replacement.

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: 1934 plan, 1939 CCC wood tower (register), 1942 wood tower (1974 article), 1958 vs 1959 steel tower, and a 1932-33 road vs 1934 road crews. Current staffing and access are unknown; the latest staffing note is a 2012 photo caption. The county agenda item is dated June 9, 2015 (Board Agenda Date), and the story gives that date. No public access info found, so no access key. The register's 2018 photos were not captured as image URLs, so no photos added.
